scope: Theorem 3.2 (Paškūnas–Tung) of the manuscript “Unrestricted pro-modularity at the prime two” (preprints/Unrestricted-pro-modularity-at-the-prime-two-October-6-2026/two-adic-promodularity.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 010 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 ef74b48557930663), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 11. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The following statements hold for every such block at p = 2, including the block of a scalar residual Galois representation. 1. The functor Hom(P, −) is an exact equivalence from the compact block to right pseudocompact E-modules, with inverse −b ⊗EP. The algebra E is finite over R. 2. Let CHR be the universal Cayley–Hamilton algebra for the local pseudorepresentation, and let CHtf R be its maximal O-torsion-free quotient. There is an R-compatible identification CHtf R ≃ ( (eEe)op, in a nonsupersingular block, M2((eEe)op), in a supersingular block. The corner equivalence is induced by the Montréal functor on the quotient by the objects with trivial SL2(Q2)-action. 3. An E-module finite and torsion-free over O gives, after duality and inversion of 2, an admissible Banach representation of finite length. At an absolutely irreducible Galois coefficient parameter there is a unique absolutely irreducible Banach object. At a sum of characters γ1 + γ2, the simple objects have the following description. If the characters coincide, the unique simple is IndG B(1 ⊗ ε−1)cts ⊗ γ1 ◦ det. If their sum is γ + γε, the simples are {1, c St, IndG B(ε ⊗ ε−1 )cts } ⊗ γ ◦ det, where c St is continuous Steinberg. If γ1γ−1 2 / ∈ {1, ε, ε−1}, they are exactly IndG B(γ1 ⊗ γ2ε−1 )cts , IndG B(γ2 ⊗ γ1ε−1 )cts . Here B is the upper Borel, induction is unnormalized, and Galois characters are viewed as characters of Q× 2 by reciprocity.
